facts.statement: The genus Belantsea was described by Lund in 1989.
Belantsea lived during the Lower Carboniferous period.
The species Ctenopetalus occidentalis is a synonym of Belantsea occidentalis.
facts.quote: synonyms: *Ctenopetalus occidentalis St. John and Worthen, 1875

facts.statement: The name Belantsea honors a legendary ancestor of the Crow Tribe.
facts.quote: Belantsea (named after a legendary ancestor of the Crow Tribe)

facts.statement: Fossils of Belantsea montana were found in the Bear Gulch Limestone lagerstätte.
facts.quote: Fossils of Belantsea montana have been found in the Bear Gulch Limestone lagerstätte

facts.statement: Researchers think Belantsea was adapted for living in sponge reefs based on its body shape.
facts.quote: This body plan suggests a lifestyle similar to modern reef fish, and it is thought that Belantsea was adapted for life in reefs of sponges

facts.statement: Belantsea likely ate hard-shelled marine invertebrates, indicated by its few large triangular teeth.
facts.quote: Its few, large, triangular teeth suggest a diet of hard-shelled marine invertebrates

facts.statement: Belantsea lived from the Lower Carboniferous to the Upper Permian.
Belantsea belongs to the class Chondrichthyes.
Belantsea is part of the family Belantseidae.
Belantsea went extinct during the Permian-Triassic mass extinction.
facts.quote: desapareció en la extinción masiva del Pérmico-Triásico

facts.statement: Belantsea had a unique appearance that resembled a bony fish rather than a cartilaginous one.
facts.quote: Se caracterizaba por tener una forma singular, ya que parecía un pez óseo en vez de un pez cartilaginoso

facts.statement: Belantsea ate ancient sponges, brachiopods, crinoids, crustaceans, and small fish.
facts.quote: Se alimentaba de esponjas ancestrales, braquiópodos, crinoideos, crustáceos y peces pequeños

facts.statement: Belantsea lived between 326.9 and 264.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Serpukhovian to Wordian (326.9 to 264.9 million years ago)
